summary: The gain-engineered transmon realizes a noise-biased qubit in a standard transmon-cavity system by adding a single microwave tone that creates frequency-selective single-photon gain on the $|e\rangle$–$|f\rangle$ transition, suppressing relaxation errors while preserving coherent control. The $|g\rangle$–$|f\rangle$ encoding achieves $T_1 = 2.22$ ms (×16.7 enhancement over $|g\rangle$–$|e\rangle$) with $T_2^E = 65$ µs and 99.58% gate fidelity, enabling scalable noise-biased error correction.
motivation: Engineering noise bias—where one error channel dominates—enables tailored QEC codes with fewer physical qubits, but previous approaches required specialized circuit elements that limited scalability. This work addresses whether noise bias can be engineered in a standard transmon architecture compatible with high-fidelity gates.
method: A parametric pump at frequency $\omega_\mathrm{gain} = (\omega_a - \alpha + \omega_b - 2\chi)/2$ activates four-wave mixing, creating a two-mode squeezing interaction that coherently couples $|e,0\rangle$ and $|f,1\rangle$ with strength $g_\mathrm{gain} = \alpha\lambda|\xi_\mathrm{gain}|^2$. Cavity photon loss ($\kappa_b$) renders this unidirectional, producing engineered gain at rate $\kappa_\mathrm{gain} = 8g_\mathrm{gain}^2/\kappa_b$ acting as a frequency-selective dissipator that drives $|e\rangle \to |f\rangle$ without affecting computational states. Two-photon drives ($\omega_a - \alpha/2$) enable fast $|g\rangle$–$|f\rangle$ gates.
result: At $g_\mathrm{gain}/2\pi = 133$ kHz ($\kappa_\mathrm{gain}/2\pi = 165$ kHz), the gain-engineered transmon achieves $T_{1,f} = 2.22(\pm0.06)$ ms and $T_{1,g} = 1.67(\pm0.34)$ ms—×14.7 average enhancement over $T_{1,e}$—with $T_2^E_{gf} = 65(\pm4)$ µs (only 2.1× shorter than $T_2^E_{ge}$) and single-qubit fidelity $\mathcal{F} = 99.58\pm0.01\%$; simulations identify thermal population and off-resonant excitations as limiting factors, suggesting improvements via better thermalization and higher cavity loss rates.
